questions.question: What happens if a parent uses `<app-fund-card />` without binding an input declared as `name = input.required<string>()`?
options: Angular logs a warning in development only
The template fails to compile because a required input is missing
questions.explanation: `input.required()` makes the binding mandatory at compile time, replacing the old `@Input() name!: string` non-null assertion.

questions.question: A child component needs to update a value the parent owns, using `[(quantity)]` syntax. Which API should the child use?
questions.explanation: `model()` creates a writable signal plus a matching `quantityChange` output, which is what two-way `[( )]` binding needs.

questions.question: Why use `linkedSignal` for a 'selected plan' that should reset when the `plans` input changes?
options: It is the only way to read an input signal
It is writable locally but automatically recomputes from its source when the source changes, avoiding effect-based syncing
It caches HTTP responses across components
It converts an Observable into a signal
questions.explanation: `computed()` is read-only and syncing with `effect()` is an anti-pattern. `linkedSignal` derives its value from a source but can still be set by the user.

questions.question: Which statement about `resource()` and `httpResource()` is accurate as of Angular 20?
options: They are stable and replace HttpClient entirely
They are experimental; they re-run the loader when their reactive params change and abort the previous request
They only work in NgModule-based apps
questions.explanation: Both are still experimental (the `request` option was already renamed to `params`). httpResource is built on HttpClient, so interceptors still apply.
